title: Wholesome One-Pot Egyptian Lamb Tagine
description: A rich and flavorful one-pot dish originating from Egypt, featuring tender lamb and silky sauce made with ssamjang and mantecada emulsification, suitable for diabetic-friendly diets.
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb shoulder on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove the lamb and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Return the lamb to the pot, cover, and transfer to the oven. Braise the lamb at 300°F (150°C) for 2 hours, or until tender.
Remove the pot from the oven and stir in the ssamjang and mantecada. Simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the fresh parsley and serve hot.
Serve the lamb in the flavorful sauce, garnished with additional parsley if desired.
Serve with couscous or rice, if desired.
Adjust the seasoning as needed before serving.
Save leftovers for up to 3 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Reheat gently before serving.
Freeze for up to 3 months in an airtight container or freezer bag. Reheat from frozen in the oven or on the stovetop, covered, until hot and steamy.
Cook poultry to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F before serving.
